claims.claim: Services are commonly distinguished from goods by four characteristics — intangibility, inseparability of production and consumption, heterogeneity (variability), and perishability — summarized as IHIP by Zeithaml, Parasuraman and Berry (1985).
In the SERVQUAL tradition, service quality is conceptualized as the gap between the service a customer expected and the service they perceived, following the expectancy-disconfirmation paradigm.

Parasuraman, Zeithaml and Berry's 1985 conceptual paper proposed ten determinants of service quality, which their 1988 Journal of Retailing paper consolidated into five dimensions: reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, and responsiveness (RATER).

The Gaps model locates the customer's expectation-perception gap (Gap 5) as the result of four internal gaps: the listening gap (1), the standards/design gap (2), the delivery/performance gap (3), and the communication gap (4).

Jan Carlzon, president of Scandinavian Airlines (SAS), popularized the term 'moment of truth' for each customer contact, estimating SAS was 'created' in customers' minds about fifty million times a year in roughly fifteen-second encounters (about 10 million customers times about 5 employee contacts).

SERVQUAL is debated: Cronin and Taylor (1992) argued that a performance-only measure (SERVPERF) predicts service quality better than the expectations-minus-perceptions difference score, and the difference-score approach has been criticized.

Service standards are specific, often measurable expectations for defined tasks, while a service culture supplies shared values and empowerment for situations standards do not anticipate; both are needed for consistent quality.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether SERVQUAL's expectations-minus-perceptions difference score is the best way to measure service quality.
positions: Parasuraman, Zeithaml and Berry (1988): quality is captured by the gap between expectations and perceptions across five dimensions.
Cronin and Taylor (1992): a performance-only measure (SERVPERF) has better predictive validity than the difference score, and difference scores raise psychometric problems.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Presented in the lesson as an open, attributed debate; SERVQUAL is taught as a widely used framework, not a settled formula, with the SERVPERF critique noted.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Attribution of the 'moment of truth' concept.
positions: The term is most widely credited to Jan Carlzon's 1987 book Moments of Truth.
The service-marketing concept is often traced to Richard Normann, whom Carlzon drew on.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson attributes popularization to Carlzon (per the assignment) while noting he developed it from Normann's work, avoiding a false claim of sole origination.

sourceRecords.title: Moments of Truth
sourceRecords.notes: Carlzon's 1987 book (English translation of the 1985 Swedish 'Riv pyramiderna!'), which popularized the 'moment of truth' concept and the ~50-million-contacts-a-year SAS calculation, and argued for empowering frontline staff. Facts cross-checked against the Wikipedia biography and multiple management summaries; the book is copyrighted and REFERENCE_ONLY. Note Carlzon drew the concept from Richard Normann.
